record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: For shift radix systems, where an SRS parameter vector r = (r_0, ..., r_{d-1}) is one for which every integer sequence satisfying 0 <= r_0 a_n + ... + r_{d-1} a_{n+d-1} + a_{n+d} < 1 eventually reaches the all-zero cycle, is the region of all SRS parameter vectors connected?

evidence.quote: The vector (r0, r1, . . . , rd−1) ∈ Rd gives a shift radix system, SRS

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\ge 1$ and a parameter vector $\mathbf{r}=(r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1})\in\mathbb{R}^d$, define the mapping $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^d$ by
$$\tau_{\mathbf{r}}(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1}) = (a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{d-1},-\lfloor r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+\cdots+r_{d-1}a_{d-1}\rfloor),$$
so that iteration of $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}$ produces an integer sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ satisfying
$$0\le r_0 a_n+r_1 a_{n+1}+\cdots+r_{d-1}a_{n+d-1}+a_{n+d}<1$$
for every $n\ge 0$. Say that $\mathbf{r}$ defines a shift radix system (SRS) with the finiteness property if, for every initial vector in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, repeated application of $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}$ eventually reaches $(0,0,\ldots,0)$. Let
$$\mathcal{D}_d^{(0)} := \{\mathbf{r}\in\mathbb{R}^d : \mathbf{r}\text{ defines an SRS with the finiteness property}\}.$$
Determine whether $\mathcal{D}_d^{(0)}$ is a connected subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on shift radix systems report that the finiteness-property set $\mathcal{D}_2^{(0)}$ in dimension two is known to be disconnected, with its largest connected component having nontrivial fundamental group; the topology of $\mathcal{D}_d^{(0)}$ in higher dimensions remains unresolved and is listed among the open problems in the SRS literature.

status_evidence.title: Shift Radix Systems - A Survey (Kirschenhofer, Thuswaldner)
status_evidence.snippet: the finiteness property set DN(2) is disconnected and ... the largest connected component has nontrivial fundamental group
status_evidence.claim: The connectedness question is settled negatively in dimension 2 but the general topological structure of the SRS region remains open.

status_evidence.title: Characterisation results for shift radix systems (Surer)
status_evidence.snippet: The boundary of D_d is very difficult to describe ... it is hard to decide whether it belongs to D_d or not.
status_evidence.claim: Topology and boundary structure of the SRS region D_d is the subject of ongoing investigation.
